chapter: Jack Laine and the New Orleans scene
title: Kids' band with Jack Laine, Millenberg and the Brunies boys
summary: As a teen he played in Jack Laine's kids band, paid a dollar or so, with George Brunies and Pansy Laine, going out to Millenberg on the Smoky Mary.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Did you all have a kids band?
Well, we had a kids band with Jack Lane.
I mean, youngsters?
Yes, all the old short pants.
I'll be doggone.

Oh, yeah. George Brunus was in that band and Pansy Lane, Jack's son, and myself. I don't know just who else. But you see... About how old were you then? Oh, I was about 14. Jack lived on Port Street. And we used to go down there and stay overnight. We'd play a job Saturday night and stay at his house. And then we'd catch the Smokey Mary on a Sunday morning and go out and play at Millenburg. When you were kids at it?
Yeah, sure. Did you get paid?
Sure we got paid. How much? Oh, a dollar, a dollar and a half. That's all anybody got.
Did they give you something to eat and something to drink, beer and stuff like that?

Well, no, they wouldn't give us any beer, because at that time they wouldn't give any kids anything that was alcoholic. They'd give you all that popping stuff, you know, cream soda and the big old fresh and butter.
Oh, you could eat there on that Millenburg, huh?
Oh, sure. Well, incidentally, that's where Jack Lane got the name Papa Lane and Mama Lane.
Putting the kids up.
Yeah, yeah. Or George Brunus used to go sleep up in the loft.
Sure. Wasn't he playing an alto then?

No, you see, they all started, those fellas all started, there wasn't any of those boys in that family that played any string instruments. They played all brass. And they used to, well, they had a band, do you remember the Detroit's, Johnny Detroit and Paul? Well, they used to parade in Dust Street out there with a wash tub for a big strum. And I think that, uh, didn't they live up around the, uh,
Arabella Street barn? You mean the Detroit's?

No, the, uh, Brunus's. Brunus's? No. At that time the old man had a place on Chappatula Street, a saloon. And the Brunus's, uh, Chappatula's in what? Well, that was between Josephine and Jackson. And I'm pretty sure that the Brunus's lived on Josephine Street. And they're in the same neighborhood, huh? Oh, yeah. On the Irish Channel? Yeah, yeah. We used to go up there and
rehearsal in the old man's saloon. Well, my memory of those kids of the Brunus's, the two, the two that I knew just by sight, was that one of them played an alto and the other one played a trumpet.

Well, Georgie played alto and he played baritone. He did? Yes, he was a little kid. He used to march in the bands, playing baritone. Incidentally, I used to play drum. You did, huh? Yeah, that's something you didn't know. Oh, I sure did.
Well, wasn't there one of those Brunus's that was so small they called him Stick Pin?
